stem: An 18-year-old transferred from paediatric to adult diabetes care 6 months ago, has not engaged with the adult team, and now presents with diabetic ketoacidosis; which outcome of poor transition does this most closely illustrate?

options.text: Ineffective or delayed transition can lead to loss of illness control and emergency presentation with a life-threatening condition
Adult transfer should routinely be postponed until the late 20s
Emergency presentations after transfer usually indicate improved self-management
Poor transition mainly affects appointment paperwork rather than health outcomes
Delayed transition is generally associated with fewer secondary complications

explanation: Ineffective or delayed transition can lead to loss of illness control and emergency presentation with a life-threatening condition, such as diabetic ketoacidosis.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf

optionExplanations.A: Correct because ineffective or delayed transition can result in loss of illness control and emergency presentation with a life-threatening condition such as diabetic ketoacidosis.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because adult transfer is meant to be planned and supported, not routinely delayed until the late 20s.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because emergency presentations after transfer usually reflect poorer control and reduced continuity of care, not improved self-management.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because poor transition can have major clinical consequences, not just administrative ones.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because delayed transition is associated with worse outcomes, including more secondary complications, not fewer.
